Why people move here

Privacy and schools, without leaving LA behind

Calabasas sits at the western edge of the San Fernando Valley, tucked into the foothills of the Santa Monica Mountains. People don't stumble into Calabasas — they choose it, usually for three reasons: the Las Virgenes Unified School District, the guard-gated privacy, and the feeling that the city still breathes — wide streets, trailheads, and open ridgelines instead of density.

It's also a working crossroads: the 101 puts Woodland Hills, Agoura Hills, and Westlake Village minutes away, Malibu Canyon Road drops you to the coast, and Old Topanga Canyon Road winds toward Topanga and the Westside. My office is right here in Calabasas at Park Sorrento — this is the market I work from every day.

Daily life

What weekends actually look like

The Commons at Calabasas

The city's living room — open-air shops, restaurants, a movie theater, and the famous turtle-and-fountain pond where the whole town seems to cross paths on a Saturday morning. The Saturday farmers market sets up nearby on Calabasas Road.

Calabasas Lake

A private, non-motorized lake ringed by homes with their own docks. If your deed includes lake rights, the walking path, fishing, and paddle boats come with the address — a lifestyle you can't buy into from outside the community.

Trails & open space

Las Virgenes Canyon, Cheeseboro/Palo Comado, and Malibu Creek State Park — the “Rock Pool” park — are all at the city's edges. Morning hikes and evening ridge sunsets are part of the rent you pay to live here, in the best way.

Schools — the quiet engine of demand

Las Virgenes Unified School District

Families routinely move to Calabasas specifically for LVUSD, consistently ranked among California's top public districts. Attendance is assigned by exact address — always verify a specific home's assigned schools with the district before you buy.

Elementary

  • Bay Laurel Elementary
  • Chaparral Elementary
  • Lupin Hill Elementary
  • Round Meadow Elementary (located in Hidden Hills)

Middle

  • Alice C. Stelle Middle School
  • Arthur E. Wright Middle School

High

  • Calabasas High School — the district flagship, known for academics, athletics, and college placement

Private options nearby

  • Viewpoint School (K–12, in Calabasas)
  • Louisville High School (Woodland Hills)
  • Sierra Canyon (Chatsworth, nearby)

Private admissions are competitive and separate from home purchase — start those applications early.

Calabasas has no single “price.” Condos near the lake are the entry point; The Oaks and its Estates sit at the top of the local market. Citywide medians land roughly between $2.2M and $2.5M depending on the source and the month's mix of sales.

Buying or selling here

Three things that decide a Calabasas deal

01

Gate, HOA & lake rights

Almost every community carries HOA dues, and they buy very different things — guard staffing, clubhouses, or lake access. I pull the HOA docs and confirm exactly what transfers with the home before we write.

02

Insurance & hillside reality

Brush-zone and hillside homes need early, real insurance quotes — not day-25 surprises. We check insurability, defensible space, and any canyon or drainage considerations up front.

03

School verification by address

District lines don't follow city limits or community names exactly. We verify the assigned LVUSD schools for the specific address in writing, so the premium you're paying is the one you actually get.

Selling in Calabasas?

Pricing here is comp-by-comp inside your own gate — a citywide median won't price your house. Start with a real valuation of your specific home, then a prep and launch plan built for your community's buyer pool. Straight answers

Calabasas questions, answered

Is Calabasas a good place to live?

For buyers who want privacy, top public schools, and a quieter, outdoors-oriented pace without leaving Los Angeles County, yes — it's one of the most deliberately chosen cities in the region. Trade-offs are real: prices are among the highest in the Valley area, most daily life is car-based, and many communities carry HOA dues and gate rules.

What is the median home price in Calabasas?

Citywide medians in 2026 land roughly between $2.2M and $2.5M depending on the source and whether you're looking at list or sold prices — Realtor.com put the median listing price at $2,495,000 in May 2026. The range inside the city is enormous: condos from around $650K to Estates at The Oaks above $20M.

What school district serves Calabasas?

The Las Virgenes Unified School District (LVUSD) — Bay Laurel, Chaparral, and Lupin Hill elementaries, A.E. Wright and Alice C. Stelle middle schools, and Calabasas High School. Assignment is by exact home address, so verify before buying.

Is Hidden Hills part of Calabasas?

No — Hidden Hills is its own incorporated, guard-gated city immediately next to Calabasas. It's searched alongside Calabasas constantly, shares LVUSD schools (Round Meadow Elementary sits inside it), and functions as part of the same luxury market, but it has its own city government and equestrian character.

How far is Calabasas from Malibu and Los Angeles?

About 20 minutes to Malibu beaches via Malibu Canyon Road, roughly 30–45 minutes to the Westside via the 101/405 or Topanga Canyon off-peak, and minutes to Woodland Hills, Agoura Hills, and Westlake Village along the 101 corridor. Peak-hour Valley traffic is the honest caveat on every one of those numbers.

Who is a good realtor in Calabasas?

Look for an agent whose office and daily work are actually in Calabasas, who can price inside your specific gate from live comps, and who handles HOA, insurance, and school-verification details before you write an offer. Daniel Smith (Sold By Mr Smith) works from First Team's Calabasas office at 24025 Park Sorrento, Suite 217, and helps buyers and sellers across Calabasas and the surrounding Valley — call 310-570-3057.

Are there homes under $1 million in Calabasas?

Yes, at the condo and townhome level, mostly near Lake Calabasas and the Park Sorrento area — expect roughly $650K and up in 2026, with HOA dues as part of the true monthly cost. Single-family homes under $1M are rare in 91302.
